claims.text: OLLAMA_HOST is neither read for routing nor written anywhere here
claims.why: The function body uses only the ollama_host parameter and DEFAULT_BENCH_OLLAMA_HOST; no environment read or write.

claims.text: the local flag is a property of the RESOLVED host rather than of the provider's name
claims.why: local is set to bool(getattr(a, 'local', False)) on the adapter, which for Ollama is derived from _is_local_http(host).

claims.text: a probe sent there is egress and is labelled as such on every record it produces
claims.why: The Lane carries local=False for non-local hosts, and grade() and _run_lane() pass lane.local into ProbeResult.

claims.text: Subclasses the council's refusal ON PURPOSE
claims.why: class LiveCanaryRefused(LiveCouncilRefused) is declared.

claims.text: a caller that wants to treat both the same writes except LiveCouncilRefused and cannot miss one of them
claims.why: Inheritance means LiveCanaryRefused is a LiveCouncilRefused.

claims.text: Three places, because default_lanes is not the only way to build a Lane
claims.why: The function checks lane.adapter, ask.__self__, and ask.__closure__.

claims.text: ask.__self__, for a bound method of an adapter
claims.why: getattr(ask, '__self__', None) is passed to _keep.

claims.text: ask.__closure__, which is where _bind keeps its adapter
claims.why: The function iterates ask.__closure__ and inspects cell_contents.

claims.text: Finding NOTHING means ask is a plain caller-supplied callable, and the verdict for that is deliberately the same one session.live_egress_seats already gives an unrecognised class
claims.why: The session.live_egress_seats implementation is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The classification itself is NOT done here -- it is session.live_egress_seats, imported
claims.why: The function calls live_egress_seats(_adapters_behind(lane)) and does not reimplement classification.

claims.text: this function only resolves a lane back to its adapter(s) and prefixes the lane's identity
claims.why: It builds f"{lane.vendor}/{lane.model} {seat}" strings.

claims.text: The checker runs ONLY on status == "ok": grading the body of a reply we never received would manufacture a wrong_answer out of an outage
claims.why: The non-ok branch returns early; probe.check is only called in the else path.

claims.text: Sequential within a lane on purpose
claims.why: _run_lane uses a for loop over probes without spawning sub-threads.

claims.text: It is also what keeps a hung vendor to ONE occupied slot rather than four
claims.why: The gate is held for the entire loop, so one lane occupies one permit.

claims.text: Threads are DAEMONS and are ABANDONED at the wall clock rather than joined
claims.why: Threads are created with daemon=True and joined with a timeout; no kill or force-join.

claims.text: Every abandoned (lane, probe) is still reported -- as timeout/wall_clock
claims.why: Boxes without a result get status='timeout' and reason='wall_clock'.

claims.text: live is the SPEND OPT-IN and defaults to False
claims.why: The parameter has default False and the gate checks `if not live`.

claims.text: Any lane that still carries a shipped vendor transport raises LiveCanaryRefused here -- before the run id, before a nonce, before a thread, before one byte is dispatched
claims.why: The raise occurs before _new_run_id(), before nonce_factory is called, and before threads are created.

claims.text: Fake lanes are unaffected, so the offline harness never has to ask for permission it does not need
claims.why: Only lanes with live_egress_seats results raise; offline adapters are not in that set.

claims.text: Materialised ONCE, before anything inspects it
claims.why: lanes = tuple(lanes) is the first statement before the gate iterates it.

claims.text: a refusal after the probes were built is still a refusal, but a refusal after dispatch is not one
claims.why: The live check precedes thread creation and dispatch.

claims.text: Prompt sizes are computed by BUILDING a sample body
claims.why: The dry_run_plan body is truncated; only the docstring's first sentence is present.

claims.text: Calls nothing -- no lane.ask is touched
claims.why: The body is truncated; cannot verify absence of ask calls.

observations.what: The live gate raises before run_id is generated, so a refused run has no run id and append_history cannot be called with it.
The wall-clock join uses deadline - time.monotonic(), which may be negative if all threads finished early; join with a negative timeout returns immediately.
The error reply in _run_lane truncates the exception string but does not include the exception class name separately beyond the prefix; the reason field is always 'bad_response'.
The gate is held for the full sequential loop, so a single lane blocks one permit for the entire wall clock; the semaphore count is max_parallel, so max_parallel lanes can run concurrently.
The plan list is built before threads start, so the result collection order is deterministic and matches the lane/probe order.
The dry_run_plan docstring is truncated mid-sentence, so its full claims cannot be evaluated.

risks: run_canary | low | A refused run has no run id, so any downstream code expecting a run id for the refusal will see nothing; inspect the caller to see if the exception carries enough context.
run_canary | low | The join timeout can be negative if all threads finish early, but join handles negative timeouts as immediate return; no defect, but the arithmetic is odd.
_run_lane | low | The error reply reason is always 'bad_response' and the exception type is only in the reply text; consumers parsing reason cannot distinguish exception types.
run_canary | low | The semaphore is held for the entire lane, so a lane that finishes early releases its permit only at the end; concurrency is limited by lane count, not probe count.
dry_run_plan | low | The docstring is truncated in this chunk, so claims about building sample bodies cannot be verified here.
